args.description:
Search online / fetch the July 2, 1959 US standards for grades of processed fruits, vegetables, and certain other products (or CFR / USDA document), and find:
1. All items listed in the "dried and dehydrated" section (or products listed as dehydrated / dried and dehydrated).
2. Specifically identify items marked as "dehydrated".
3. Check the "Frozen" or "Frozen/Chilled" section for any items that contain the whole name of those items, excluding any marked "Chilled".
4. Determine the effective dates / version dates given in the 1959 standards for these items.
5. Check current (as of August 2023) USDA AMS standards for grades of processed fruits and vegetables to see which of these standards have been superseded by a new version since the 1959 date.
6. Return full details of all matched items, their 1959 dates, their current status / latest version dates, and the calculation of superseded percentage.
args.output_contract: Detailed report of the search results, list of items meeting criteria, dates in 1959 standard, current status as of Aug 2023, whether superseded, and percentage calculation.

args.summary:
We analyzed the July 2, 1959 USDA standards document ("United States standards for grades of processed fruits, vegetables, and certain other products (as of July 2, 1959)").

1. In the "DRIED or DEHYDRATED" section, exactly 3 items are specifically marked as dehydrated:
   - Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) (Effective Nov 29, 1955)
   - Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) (Effective March 19, 1956)
   - Orange Juice (Dehydrated) (Effective Jan 27, 1956)

2. In the "FROZEN or CHILLED" section (excluding items marked Chilled):
   - Only 1 item contains the whole name of one of these items: "Apples" (Effective May 17, 1954). Neither "Grapefruit Juice" nor "Orange Juice" appears on its own (only "Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated", "Orange Juice, Concentrated", and blends).
